# Hublot

> One real, visible Chromium window shared by any number of AI agents, each through its own
> tab, with a plain CLI and no MCP session to pre-configure. Open source (BZ-1.1 License), a
> BREIZHZION project.

Playwright MCP works well for a single agent, but not several at once: one agent owns the
browser session, and an MCP server has to be declared before the agent's session even starts.
Skipping the MCP layer for a raw Playwright script or CLI does not solve this either, since
Playwright's own tooling is one-shot by design and nothing keeps a browser window alive between
two separate shell commands. Hublot's broker is a small process that stays resident in the
background, keeps the browser and its tabs alive, and answers one command at a time over a
local socket, so any agent can call `hublot open`/`click`/`type`/`screenshot` at any moment
without pre-wiring anything.

## Documentation
- [Site vitrine](https://hublot.breizhzion.com): présentation, architecture, commandes, installation
- [Dépôt source](https://github.com/bzhzion/hublot): code TypeScript/Node.js, releases, issues, licence BZ-1.1

## Optional
- [Releases](https://github.com/bzhzion/hublot/releases): exécutable Windows signé (Azure Trusted Signing) et paquet Debian
